title: Computational geodynamics and the evolving Earth
blurb: A progression from mantle convection and plate tectonics to open, self-describing computational geoscience.

person.name: Louis Moresi
person.affiliation: Australian National University, Research School of Earth Sciences
person.expertise: Geodynamics, mantle convection, computational mechanics, scientific software, and reproducible geoscience

sources.title: ANU research profile and software lineage

papers.title: The large-scale structure of convection in the earth's mantle

notes.takeaway: Seismic tomography connects mantle-scale circulation with surface plate motions, while exchange across the upper–lower mantle boundary remains contested.
notes.why: Start with the observations a convection model must explain.

notes.takeaway: Three-dimensional models expose how geometry, viscosity, heating, and boundary assumptions change the predicted circulation.
notes.why: Establish what numerical experiments add to scaling arguments.

papers.title: Mantle convection with a brittle lithosphere: thoughts on the global tectonic styles of the Earth and Venus

notes.takeaway: Changing lithospheric yield strength produces stagnant, mobile, or episodically overturning lids in temperature-dependent convection models.
notes.why: Moresi and Solomatov connect failure mechanics to contrasting planetary tectonic styles.

papers.title: Mantle Convection Modeling with Viscoelastic/Brittle Lithosphere: Numerical Methodology and Plate Tectonic Modeling

notes.takeaway: A particle-in-cell finite-element formulation couples large-deformation viscoelasticity with strain-dependent yielding and checks accuracy against analytic benchmarks.
notes.why: Follow the transition from a viscous mantle to a lithosphere with elastic memory and brittle failure.

papers.title: A Lagrangian integration point finite element method for large deformation modeling of viscoelastic geomaterials

notes.takeaway: An Eulerian mesh solves field variables while moving integration particles retain material history through large deformation.
notes.why: This explains the numerical machinery behind evolving, history-dependent geomaterials.

papers.title: Simulating faults and plate boundaries with a transversely isotropic plasticity model

notes.takeaway: Transversely isotropic plasticity represents the directional weakness of unresolved fault surfaces and promotes asymmetric subduction in the modeled cases.
notes.why: Ask how small-scale fault physics can enter a mantle-scale calculation without resolving every shear band.

papers.title: Computational approaches to studying non-linear dynamics of the crust and mantle

notes.takeaway: The formulation, solution strategy, and parallel implementation are developed together for nonlinear viscoelastic-plastic crust and mantle dynamics.
notes.why: Connect mathematical assumptions to the architecture of a working research solver.

papers.title: Underworld2: Python Geodynamics Modelling for Desktop, HPC and Cloud

notes.takeaway: Underworld2 packages geodynamics modeling in a Python-facing environment spanning desktop, high-performance, and cloud computing.
notes.why: Use the reviewed software paper as the entry point to the implementation and its archived release.

papers.title: Underworld3: Mathematically Self-Describing Modelling in Python for Desktop, HPC and Cloud

notes.takeaway: Underworld3 expresses model mathematics symbolically and generates the machinery used to discretize and solve it.
notes.why: Follow the software lineage from numerical implementation to models whose mathematical structure can be inspected at runtime.

notes.takeaway: Three-dimensional models trace how buoyant crustal accretion disrupts subduction, drives lateral trench rollback, and reorganizes the convergent margin.
notes.why: Moresi and colleagues connect dynamic experiments to geological evidence from eastern Australia.

papers.title: Subduction invasion polarity switch from the Pacific to the Atlantic Ocean: A new geodynamic model of subduction initiation based on the Scotia Sea region

notes.takeaway: Reconstructions and numerical experiments test a proposed polarity-switch mechanism for new subduction in the Scotia region.
notes.why: Treat subduction initiation as a competing-mechanisms problem, not a settled inference from one reconstruction.

papers.title: Subduction dynamics and overriding plate deformation

notes.takeaway: Subduction-zone width and maturity alter slab motion, mantle return flow, and whether the overriding plate extends or shortens.
notes.why: A recent synthesis links model behavior to comparisons across active subduction zones.

sections.label: Foundations: mantle convection
sections.summary: Geodynamics begins with mantle flow, heat transport, and the large-scale structure of convection. These models establish the physical processes that later work connects to plate motions and geological history.

sections.label: Rheology: plates and materials
sections.summary: The field adds heterogeneous and anisotropic materials, melting, and plasticity to explain how deformation localizes. Constitutive choices determine whether a model produces Earth-like plate boundaries.

sections.label: Software: scalable computational experiments
sections.summary: Numerical methods and open codes make planetary-scale experiments possible and expose the numerical assumptions behind them. Benchmarks and reproducible examples are part of the evidence.
questions: How should geodynamic codes expose error?

sections.label: Frontier: tectonics across planets
sections.summary: Current work connects computation to subduction, overriding-plate deformation, and planetary evolution. The frontier is comparing mechanisms across scales while preserving reproducibility.
